claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous and lacks distinct nanoscale precipitates or composition undulation.
The baseline CoCrFeNi alloy has a uniform, single-phase microstructure.
A minor addition of Al, Nb, Ti, or V to CoCrFeNi can promote nanoprecipitate formation.
The proposed microalloying addition will generate a nanohierarchical architecture in the CoCrFeNi matrix during elevated-temperature sliding.
The resulting structure will comprise coupled nanoscale grains, distributed nanoprecipitates, and composition undulation.
A nanohierarchical architecture with nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates can provide adaptive friction-interface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
At lower temperatures, nanoprecipitates and coupled grains distribute frictional stress through multiple deformation pathways.
At 800 °C, the nanohierarchical architecture promotes a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The high-temperature glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
The microalloyed CoCrFeNi variant will have substantially lower wear than baseline CoCrFeNi across 25–800 °C.
The microalloyed CoCrFeNi variant may achieve wear rates on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm³/Nm.
The microalloyed CoCrFeNi variant will maintain a low coefficient of friction throughout 25–800 °C.
The proposed performance is expected under dry or minimally oxidizing sliding conditions.
The comparison should use identical load, speed, and environmental conditions for baseline and microalloyed samples.
TEM, SEM, XRD, and EDS can test whether the proposed nanoprecipitates, phases, composition distribution, and nanohierarchical architecture formed.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and coefficient of friction, or failure to observe the proposed structure, would falsify the hypothesis.
